LSL — recorded results

7 completed · 0 failed · 0 not finished. No extra processing wait is imposed in these two tests.

Example only — short cloud functionality check. Run the full configuration on your acquisition PC.

Recorded on Linux / Python 3.12.14.

Receiver reading target: 2048 Hz. Every cycle reads buffered samples from every stream. The operating system can delay a cycle; actual reading rates and gaps are listed below. Reading faster does not change sensor sampling rates.

Test 1 — EEG only

Rows are EEG channel counts. Columns are sampling rates. Each cell shows the highest measured value across repetitions. The table below keeps every run.

After send: time from the send call to the read. Sample to read: also includes waiting for the sender to fill a batch. p99: 99% of samples had a delay at or below this value. Signal difference: zero means the values match. The two marker maps compare the stored sample timing and the actual read timing separately. Colors follow each map's printed scale; they are not pass/fail categories.

Sent signal and received signal

The first plot uses every recorded sample and its carried sender time. The second is a live view on one fixed display clock: both curves keep the latest value available at each display step. It is not the full reconstruction. Empty reads retain the previous value; all samples remain saved. The delay plot uses actual read times. Curves are never shifted to fit. A faster reading loop cannot replace a higher acquisition rate.

EEG markers and the change in the signal

A, B and C cause the configured change in the sent EEG, normally 200 ms later. One color identifies each marker. Solid lines and filled symbols mean sent; dashed lines and hollow symbols mean received. Circles are markers; triangles are EEG changes. Sent times use the source sample counter; received times use the receiver read counter.

Synchronization between sensors

The same known event changes every simulated sensor. The first chart compares sample times for analysis; the second compares actual read times. Different acquisition rates can place the first changed sample slightly apart. The table separates that original difference from any added timing difference.

After viewing the results

These are recorded measurements, not an automatic diagnosis. Sample loss, delivery delay and marker timing are separate results. The simulated sensors share one sender clock; independent physical devices need their own clock synchronization measurements.

Extra tests — slow processing and recovery

Run python main.py --local --out results-extra only as a separate experiment. These tests deliberately add processing time. Recovery means the waiting data return to the initial level after that extra wait is removed, while transmission continues. A processing-time ratio of 1 uses all available time; 2 takes twice as long. These extra tests are not part of the normal LSL check above.

Files: metrics.csv, markers.csv, and recordings.zip. The archive contains the original signal arrays and the sender/receiver time vectors for reanalysis.
